statement:
Neryva exists because progress in AI depends on more than scale.

The last several years have shown that larger models, trained on more data with more compute, can produce remarkable capabilities. But that approach has limits. Training runs are fragile. Inference is expensive. Deployment is constrained by hardware, latency, and cost. And many of the gains from scale come with waste that is poorly understood and rarely measured.

We believe that the most important technical problems in AI right now are not about making systems bigger. They are about making systems more efficient, more stable, and more deployable. That means studying how computation is allocated, how training behaves under pressure, how inference can be optimized for real constraints, and how learned behavior transfers across tasks and domains.

Neryva is organized around these problems. Our primary focus is on large-scale language models, where routing, sparsity, training dynamics, and inference optimization all intersect. We also pursue related research in robotics and task transfer, safe clinical AI, and energy and engineering optimization — areas where the same concerns with efficiency, reliability, and deployment constraints apply.

We are a small lab. We choose problems carefully. We focus on work where progress can be measured, where claims can be tied to evidence, and where the research is legible enough for others to build on.
